frameworks.name: Sequential Small Battle Method
frameworks.definition: A progression where a founder wins one small battle, then one per month, then one per week, then one per day — each stage compounding relative magnitude until the founder has transformed their identity.

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that self-belief is built through a sequence of progressively smaller-interval wins — one small battle, then one per month, then one per week, then one per day — rather than from a prior history of success; the act of winning sequentially creates the identity of an entrepreneur, not the other way around.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: founder has no prior track record or has a negative track record
wins are small and concrete, not abstract
claims.mechanism: Each small win provides evidence to the actor that they are capable; as win frequency increases (monthly to weekly to daily), the subjective size of each win grows relative to what was difficult 60-90 days prior, compounding into an identity shift visible on the order of six months.

claims.text: Greg Short claims that starting a venture with a negative track record is not a disqualifier; he had no positive history when he began building what became the largest energy drink in his market, and the absence of prior success is the normal starting condition, not an exception.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: applies to first-time founders and those with prior failures

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that small wins compound and snowball over roughly six months of consistent action, such that the magnitude of each win relative to starting difficulty grows substantially — a battle that once felt large becomes comparatively small as capacity increases.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: requires consistent action — wins must occur at increasing frequency over months
applies to early-stage founders in the identity-formation phase
claims.mechanism: Repeated completion of difficult tasks re-calibrates the actor's internal reference point for difficulty; what was once hard becomes routine, freeing capacity for larger challenges and producing compounding momentum.

numbers.axis: time elapsed from starting the sequential small-battle method

anchors.value: one small battle per day — each now much larger in absolute difficulty than the first

claims.text: Greg Short claims that after approximately six months of executing the sequential small-battle method, a founder's identity visibly transforms — the person looking back in the mirror is unrecognizable from who they were at the start — and that this transformation is the output of accumulated action, not a prerequisite to it.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: requires roughly six months of consistent sequential wins
applies to people who begin with no external validation or track record
claims.mechanism: Identity is the accumulated residue of actions taken; consistent action at increasing frequency and magnitude rewrites the actor's self-model from non-entrepreneur to entrepreneur without requiring any single transformative event.

examples.text: Greg Short describes his own origin building what became the largest energy drink in his country: he did not start with a goal of achieving that scale — he started wanting to do something, anything, with a negative track record behind him. His path was a sequence of small battles taken at increasing frequency, eventually compounding over six months into an identity he no longer recognized as his original self. The energy drink scale was a downstream result of that compounding process, not the original target.

practices.text: Start by taking on one small battle. Once that is won, aim for one per month, then one per week, and eventually one per day. Do not wait for self-belief to arrive before starting — use the wins themselves as the source of belief.
